title: Restriction of scalars commutes with $j_!$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]) and $j\colon U\to X$ an open immersion. With $j_!$ the
extension by zero of module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]) there is a natural
isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ j_!\;\cong\;j_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_U}\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda'_U}\longrightarrow\Mod_{\Lambda_X}.
$$

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal C=\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $S=j^*_{\Ab}$ and $P=j^{\Ab}_!$. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], $S$ is strong monoidal and $\alpha_j:S\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$, $\alpha'_j:S\Lambda'_X\to\Lambda'_U$ are ring-object morphisms. By [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], $P$ has the projection formula $P(SL\otimes M)\cong L\otimes PM$. Denote its linearizations by $P_B:\Mod_{SB}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_B(\mathcal D)$. The same node defines $j_!^\Lambda=P_{\Lambda_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$ and $j_!^{\Lambda'}=P_{\Lambda'_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha'_j}$. Thus all functors used below have the indicated module categories as their sources and targets.

source.place: First paragraph: linearization and the definition of module extension by zero

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-projection-formula-comap] with the $S,P$ of step 1, $B=\Lambda_X$, $B'=\Lambda'_X$ and $\varphi=a_X$. It gives $\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ P_{\Lambda'_X}\cong P_{\Lambda_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{Sa_X}$, identity on underlying objects. Precompose this natural isomorphism with $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha'_j}$ and substitute the definition in step 1, obtaining $\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ j_!^{\Lambda'}\cong P_{\Lambda_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{Sa_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha'_j}$. No extension-of-scalars functor or flatness assumption is involved.

source.place: First paragraph: application with S=j^* and phi=a_X

proof.text: For composable ring-object maps $u:A\to B$, $v:B\to C$, restriction as defined in [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] gives a $C$-module with action $\gamma:C\otimes M\to M$ the action $\gamma\circ(v\otimes1)\circ(u\otimes1)=\gamma\circ((v\circ u)\otimes1)$. Both restrictions fix underlying morphisms. Consequently the identity maps give a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Res}_u\circ\operatorname{Res}_v\cong\operatorname{Res}_{v\circ u}$. Apply this with $u=Sa_X$, $v=\alpha'_j$. By [lem-sfb-coefficient-pullback-square] with $f=j$, $\alpha'_j\circ Sa_X=a_U\circ\alpha_j$. The two restrictions along these equal maps have identical actions and morphisms. Apply the same calculation with $u=\alpha_j$, $v=a_U$ to obtain $\operatorname{Res}_{Sa_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha'_j}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_U}$. Each component and its inverse is the identity on the underlying sheaf; its naturality equation for a module map $h$ is $h\circ1=1\circ h$.

source.place: Displayed composite restriction and second paragraph: coefficient square and composition of restrictions

proof.text: Postcompose the natural isomorphism of step 3 with $P_{\Lambda_X}$, and compose with that of step 2. The result is $\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ j_!^{\Lambda'}\cong P_{\Lambda_X}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_U}=j_!^\Lambda\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_U}$, where the last equality is the definition in [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. This composite is the chosen comparison. Its inverse is the reverse composite of the inverses from steps 2 and 3; their componentwise inverse equations imply those for the composite. Naturality follows by composing their naturality squares (applying $P_{\Lambda_X}$ to that of step 3). The common source is $\Mod_{\Lambda'_U}$ and common target is $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, as required.

source.place: Second paragraph, last clause: identify the final composite with j_! after restriction

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; composition of scalar restrictions and naturality expanded explicitly
